name: King of Achshaph
overview: The King of Achshaph was a male ruler identified in the Book of Joshua as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded, his defeat is noted as part of Israel's divinely guided victory. This title represents the authority he held over the city of Achshaph at that time.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Achshaph' literally means 'king of Achshaph,' indicating his rulership over the city named Achshaph. This designation is a straightforward title rather than a personal name given by God, as recorded in Joshua 11:1.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for the King of Achshaph beyond his identification as a king defeated by Joshua. No additional relational information is provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Achshaph's significance lies in his role as one of the thirty-one kings overcome by Joshua, demonstrating God's fulfillment of His promise to give Israel victory over the land of Canaan. His defeat symbolizes the comprehensive nature of Israel's conquest under divine direction, affirming God's sovereignty and faithfulness to His covenant people.
